newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua set to issue $50 mln in coffee bonds.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua set to issue $50 mln in coffee bonds.

text.p: Nicaragua's coffee growers will issue $50 million in coffee bonds by March to help finance coffee production, a top government officials said on Monday.

"We expect the bonds will be ready in March at the latest. We are carrying out a review because they have to be well-backed and supported to be sold at the international level," the Minister of Foreign Cooperation, David Robleto, told Reuters.

Robleto, previously head of Nicaragua's Union of Coffee Growers (Unicafe), originally presented the idea of the development bonds in November and said they would be issued after the new government of President Arnoldo Aleman came to power on Jan. 10.
"We are going to do it just like Guatemala and other Central American countries did it. We are going to supply the bonds to all the stock exchanges and agencies that make bonds available," he said.

Robleto said they still had not decided which investment houses would deal the bonds, but they would be available in "the United States, Europe, Central America and all markets that have stock exchanges."
He said the bonds would be redeemable in five years and likely have an annual yield of 10 percent.
The bonds, which he said will be backed by the Nicaraguan government, will provide desperately needed financing in the medium and long term to Nicaragua's capital-starved coffee growers.
